sonnet.problem: The statement bundles two claims: Joshua does what the LORD says, and he makes the knives and circumcises. It also just restates the command from card 1, so the True answer is obvious and teaches nothing new.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim. ... A True statement never just repeats the card before it.

sonnet.problem: The joke (a PAST DUE stamp coming off an account) decides that 'the reproach of Egypt' means a debt or a mark against Israel. The text never says what the reproach is, and the comparison also does not clearly match the action of rolling away.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect. This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.

sonnet.problem: Card 14 already established that Israel ate unleavened bread and roasted grain from the land, so the baker already knows they have food. Card 17 re-asks that same fact and is answerable from the earlier card.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.
